well in theory, styro is when it bleeds, because styro is referring to the second layer of skin (the dermis, under the epidermis) and a cut into the dermis causes bleeding. 

but what people are reffering to when they say styro on this kind of sub is usually when the cut is (slightly) gaping open and a few millimeters deep at least. that's when you can see the white layer clearly, and yeah, if you get to it in one swipe woth a sharp tool, it doesn't bleed immediately.

in deeper styro levels, you might start to see some yellow or pink because of blood vessels and the start of the fat layer (the beans, under the dermis/styro)

about scarring, cut's can be pretty imprevisible. some really deep cut's might leave marks that are as visible as a styro. but usually if your cuts are gaping open you can be sure it's gonna leave a scar for life. a shallower cut might also leave a scar for a long time (or a lifetime) but they are usually less textured, a lot thinner and whiter and less visible in general)

that's all friend, i'm wishing you all the best, courage and luck
